problem_checks.source: PDF p2 Definition 1.5; p3 Conjecture 1.6; p16 Theorem 5.1
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: R=F2[x,y,z]_(x,y,z) is a connected regular Noetherian local field algebra of dimension 3. The free complex in degrees 3,2,1,0 has ranks 1,1,3,1, differential d1=[x y z] and all other differentials zero. It is minimal, nonexact, and all displayed terms are nonzero. H0=k, H1=ker[x y z] contains the nonzero (y,x,0), and H2=H3=R. H1 is nonzero and torsionfree over a domain, so has full support. The codimensions on the displayed interval are 3,0,0,0 and rank sum 6<2^3. Localization at the height-three maximal ideal leaves positive-rank homology, so is not tiny.
problem_checks.quantifier_revision: The displayed maximum is read over the displayed homological interval, equivalently the nonzero homology groups in this example. If instead all outside zero groups are included with codim(0)=+infinity, no finite c is assigned to bounded complexes. The original unconditional zero-convention sentence has been replaced by these explicit alternatives.
problem_checks.counterevidence_and_repair: Tiny complexes and Theorem 4.1 explicitly require finite-length nonzero homology; this example violates that finite-length hypothesis and does not refute the restricted theorem. Replacing max by the codimension of total support, namely min over nonzero H_j, excludes the example and justifies finite-length localization at a minimal support prime. The later transfer and tiny-complex arguments remain external/retained dependencies.

problem_checks.source: PDF p3 Theorem 1.7, pp5?6 Notation 1.13, pp15?16 Theorem 4.10
problem_checks.independent_reasoning: R=F2[[x,y]] is complete, regular, dimension two, with perfect residue field. P=(R--1-->R), extended by zero, belongs to the stated finite-length-homology category but is contractible, as are all Frobenius iterates. Thus beta(P)=h_infinity(P)=h1_infinity(P)=chi_infinity(P)=0, while the displayed free-term rank sum is 2. The introductory inequality becomes 2>=4; the later ratio is 0/0, and the chi=0 clause gives 0>=2. Minimal Betti rank and raw free rank are explicitly distinguished.
